data.description:
## Report

When `review-plan` PASSES but the attestation write hits a lock timeout, it prints:

    plan review PASSED but the attestation could not be persisted: flock: could not acquire lock after 60s
    run `rebar sign-review <id>` to re-sign from the recorded review (no LLM re-run) — the claim gate needs the signature.

That guidance is only sound when the SIDECAR persisted and only the signature failed. When one contention episode takes BOTH, `sign-review` returns:

    {"ok": false, "signed": false, "verdict": "BLOCK",
     "reason": "the latest review was not a signable PASS (verdict=BLOCK) — run `rebar review-plan` to produce a fresh verdict"}

Observed twice while earning the attestation for bug royal-weariless-zebrafish; the response payload carried `"sidecar_emitted": false` both times, confirming no PASS record was written. Each occurrence cost a full ~14-minute, 28-LLM-call review.

Worse than losing the result: the recorded verdict silently remains the PREVIOUS round BLOCK, so the system retains a STALE CONTRADICTING verdict rather than no verdict.

## Suggested direction

Condition the printed guidance on `sidecar_emitted`. When the sidecar did NOT persist, say so plainly and name the real remedy (re-run `review-plan`), rather than naming a no-LLM recovery that cannot work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the sidecar failed to persist, the emitted guidance does NOT advertise `sign-review`, verified by a test asserting the message text for `sidecar_emitted=false`
- [ ] When only the signature failed, the `sign-review` guidance is still emitted, verified by a test for `sidecar_emitted=true`
- [ ] A stale prior verdict is not silently presented as current, verified by a test
data.title: sign-review advertises a recovery path that cannot work when the PASS sidecar was also lost
